changes.current_line: Billing that helps you grow revenue.
changes.change: For buyers replacing a homegrown billing system, lead with roadmap drag instead of revenue growth: 'Stop billing being a tax on the roadmap: pricing changes in minutes, not a quarter.' Product leaders' own proof point: 'a quarter of roadmap in five minutes.'
changes.why: Owen rejected the revenue framing outright ('we're not trying to grow revenue with billing') and named his real problem as 'a tax on the roadmap', where every pricing change takes a quarter.

changes.current_line: Proven ROI, backed by an independent economic impact study.
changes.change: When a champion asks for payback, respond within days with a payback number built from their own costs. Position the independent study as supporting evidence only: 'Your payback, built on your numbers, and checked against an independent economic impact study.'
changes.why: Owen asked 'do you have something that shows payback?', received the general ROI deck with the study, and said he couldn't get it past Diane without 'a number that's ours'. The session to build that number never happened.

changes.change: Create a finance-facing line on the cost of the status quo that the champion can forward to the CFO: 'What your homegrown billing costs you every quarter: engineering time, billing errors, and subscriptions that lapse when a card fails and nobody chases it.' Pair it with a short worksheet so finance reads the problem as urgent, not as a nice to have. Where failed-card lapses come up, link them to automatic recovery (M10).
changes.why: Finance saw the project as a 'nice to have' under a rule of 'if it isn't on fire, it isn't funded'. The money leaks were real (lapsed subscriptions from failed cards), but 'We never added it up.'

changes.change: For buyers migrating off a homegrown billing system, offer a peer reference: a customer who has already made the move and will talk to the buyer's product or engineering lead. Offer it alongside the migration doc, not as a substitute for it.
changes.why: We had a migration doc, but Owen 'wanted to talk to someone who'd done it', and the transcript doesn't show that a reference was ever offered.
